subject: Unexpected hourly usage spike — urgent review & VAT implication
messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@nimbushealth.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jarek Nowak <jarek.nowak@nimbushealth.eu>, Nimbus Billing <billing@nimbushealth.eu>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Unexpected hourly usage spike — urgent review & VAT implication

Hi Hannah,

We noticed a sharp spike in hourly token counts on Sep 14 that resulted in a significant mid-cycle overage on our invoice (invoice #NH-2025-0914). Our engineers traced the usage back to a cluster of requests that appear to have been double-counted during an hourly bucketing window — roughly 02:00–03:00 CEST on the 14th. The spike pushed us into the next tier and created an unexpected charge of ~€6,200.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a quick explanation of what caused the double-counting and confirm whether this is a billing-side issue (vs. our integration)?
- If it’s on Redwood’s side, we need a provisional credit and an official credit memo that includes VAT treatment for our EU entity (we’re registered in Poland, VAT ID PL524xxxxx).

I’ve attached a short CSV with example request IDs and timestamps (usage-snippet.csv). We’re holding payment for this invoice pending clarification; please advise next steps and ETA.

Thanks,
Lucia
Lucia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health
[Attachment: usage-snippet.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@nimbushealth.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 10:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected hourly usage spike — urgent review & VAT implication

Hi Lucia — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the disruption. We’ve opened a triage ticket and I looped in Karthik (billing ops) and Marissa (your account lead).

Quick notes:
- We see the usage rows you attached and will run a cross-check against our hourly aggregation logs.
- Initial hypothesis: an edge-case during the CEST daylight-savings window where a short overlap caused requests to be assigned to two hourly buckets in the aggregation pipeline.

Action items / timeline:
1) Karthik will share a provisional analysis and sample server logs by EOD tomorrow (19 Sep).
2) If the root cause is on our side, we will issue a provisional credit and follow up with a formal credit memo that includes the VAT position.
3) We’ll also propose a small one-time goodwill credit to cover the trouble while we finalize the numbers.

Can you confirm whether holding payment for the full invoice is acceptable while we investigate? If you can share the customer PO / payment reference, that helps expedite the accounting side.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Director, EMEA — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@nimbushealth.eu>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 17:28:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected hourly usage spike — preliminary analysis

Hi Lucia / Hannah — I pulled the aggregation traces for 14 Sep and matched them with the request ids in usage-snippet.csv. Preliminary findings below: 

Summary:
- There was an overlap in the hourly bucketing job that ran during a rolling update on our aggregation workers between 02:45–03:10 CEST. Two worker instances briefly processed the same partition while a re-sharding operation was in-flight, which resulted in duplicate entries for ~0.6% of requests in that hour.
- Impact on Nimbus Health: the duplicated counts are concentrated in 02:50–03:05 and together caused ~135k additional tokens to be billed in the hourly rollup (approx. €6,200).

Proposed remediation steps:
1) Immediate provisional credit: we can apply a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens (value above) to offset the disputed invoice.
2) Credit memo: accounting will issue an official credit memo (with VAT line item) once we complete a full forensic export — target within 5 business days.
3) Root cause fix: ops have deployed a fix to prevent double-processing during re-shards.

We need two things from you to finalize the credit memo:
- Confirmation of your entity VAT ID (you included PL524xxxxx — please provide full ID for the memo).
- Whether Nimbus would prefer the credit memo net of VAT or as a gross credit with VAT separately documented (this affects your reverse-charge handling).

Attachments: provisional billing-draft.pdf (stub) with the arithmetic used for the provisional credit.

I’ve set the provisional credit as pending until we validate the full export; if you want the credit applied immediately to unlock payment clearance we can do that and reconcile afterwards. Please let us know which you prefer.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: billing-draft.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@nimbushealth.eu>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jarek Nowak <jarek.nowak@nimbushealth.eu>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 08:07:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected hourly usage spike — VAT/reverse-charge question

Hi Karthik — thanks for the quick investigation and the provisional numbers. We confirm our full VAT ID is PL5241239876.

Regarding VAT treatment: Nimbus Health will handle VAT under the EU reverse-charge mechanism (we are VAT-registered in Poland and will account for VAT in our return). For the credit memo we need:
- A clear statement that the original charge will be offset and that the credit memo references invoice NH-2025-0914.
- The credit memo should include your VAT number and a note indicating reverse-charge applies (so our AP team can file correctly).

We prefer you apply the provisional credit immediately so we can release the payment hold for the remaining balance while you finalize the export.

Attaching our tax proof for your records.

Best,
Lucia
[Attachment: EU_Tax_Proof.pdf (PDF, 64KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@nimbushealth.eu>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 15:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected hourly usage spike — confirmation and next steps

Hi Lucia — appreciate the confirmation and the VAT document. We will: 

- Apply the provisional credit today (amount per Karthik’s draft) so you can release the payment hold for the remainder of the invoice.
- Issue an official credit memo that references NH-2025-0914, includes Redwood’s VAT number (GB987654321), and explicitly states reverse-charge applies. You should receive the credit memo and accounting entry within 3 business days.
- Send a short post-mortem once the full forensic export is complete (target 5 business days).

Links for your reference: HubSpot ticket https://app.hubspot.com/ticket/83452 and the DocuSign amendment we’ll use if you want the accounting team to sign an addendum: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/0a1b2c3d4e

If you want us to apply the provisional credit as a manual refund instead of a credit memo, tell us and we’ll coordinate with bookkeeping — otherwise we’ll proceed with the credit memo approach requested.

Thanks again for the partnership — we’ll keep you updated.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Director, EMEA — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal-trace-log-stub.txt (TXT, 8KB)]
